deepdive.sec: Industrial Thermal Processing & Nuclear Grade Equipment

bull_bear.body: No further equity dilution (all warrants converted); Debt levels stable despite working capital fluctuations; Cash flows expected to normalize in H1 FY27 as receivables (INR 50-60cr Moroccan, others) are collected.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tensions (Middle East/West Asia) causing logistics bottlenecks and order finalization delays (2-3 month shift); Working capital intensity (days increased to 184); Execution delays in nuclear vertical (12+ month cycles).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth and margin sustainability (22-23%); Cautiously realistic about near-term geopolitical headwinds affecting dispatch timing; Emphasized 'high aspirations' but guided conservatively (20-25%) to manage expectations.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Significant portion of 'Other Income' is operating in nature (FX gains on exports) and should be mentally added to EBITDA for true margin assessment (~80% of other income); Q4 gross margin dip driven by specific high-subcontract jobs, not structural cost creep.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Kilburn (Parent): Fertilizer (dryers), Nuclear (components), Petrochem (vapor recovery); M.E. Energy: Waste heat recovery (Steel/Ferrous Alloy focus, Cement early stage); Monga Strayfield: Textiles, Food Processing, Defrosting (RF dryers).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistics bottlenecks and delayed dispatches due to Middle East crisis impacting revenue recognition timing | Kilburn Engineering Ltd | beneficiary | High | Company has INR 4,000cr+ pipeline and capacity expansions coming online; delays are temporal (2-3 months) rather than demand destruction; strong pricing power maintains 25% margins despite chaos. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margins pressured in Q4 by high subcontracting mix and freight costs for Moroccan order; Material cost inflation (steel) mitigated by immediate booking policy; Management clarifies no automatic cost pass-through, relying on hedging at order stage.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 20-25% CAGR (Target INR 750-800cr for FY27); Margin: 20%+ (Management comfort zone 22-23%); Order Inflow: INR 800-1,000cr (FY27); Capex/Commissioning: INR 40cr total; Saravali (Kilburn) and Pune Phase 2 (M.E. Energy) expansions completing by end-Q2 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 467cr consolidated backlog; Inquiry pipeline >INR 4,000cr across fertilizer, nuclear, petrochem, steel; Expectation to close INR 450-500cr of new orders by end-Q2 FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Nuclear sector re-entry (2 projects in pipeline, Kaiga); Export market expansion targeting 30-40% revenue mix (US, Europe, Far East); Cement sector breakthrough for WHRB systems.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Kilburn delivered strong FY26 consolidated growth (Revenue INR 629cr, +~50% YoY implied) with robust 25% EBITDA margins, though Q4 cash flow was temporarily negative due to lumpy dispatches (INR 130cr) and Middle East logistics delays. Guidance remains constructive for 20-25% revenue CAGR to reach INR 1,000cr by FY28, underpinned by a INR 4,000cr+ inquiry pipeline and near-term capacity expansions, despite near-term order finalization slippages.
